script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

INT. OFFICE BUILDING - DAY

A bustling office building. PASSIONATE EMPLOYEES move quickly from desk to desk, heads buried in computers, fingers tapping keys.

INT. HR OFFICE - DAY

A MAN in his 40s, JAMES, sits nervously outside the HR office. His resume clutched tightly in his hands. He looks up as the HR REPRESENTATIVE, SARAH, opens the door.

SARAH
(friendly)
James, come in. Have a seat.

James follows Sarah into her office, sitting across the desk from her.

JAMES
(nervously)
Thank you for seeing me, Sarah. I really want this job.

SARAH
(smiling)
We want you too, James. But there's something we need to discuss.

INT. HR OFFICE - FLASHBACK - YEARS AGO

James, younger and more carefree, stands with SARAH in the same HR office. They laugh and talk, clearly friends.

SARAH
(laughing)
I'll put in a good word for you, James. This job's a great opportunity.

JAMES
(grinning)
Thanks, Sarah. I won't let you down.

INT. HR OFFICE - PRESENT

Back in the present, Sarah delivers the news that James had been fired from his last job due to poor performance.

SARAH
(firmly)
I'm sorry, James. We can't offer you the position without addressing that issue.

JAMES
(deflated)
I know. I understand.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

James sits alone at a table, staring at his phone. He looks up as it rings. It's Sarah.

JAMES
(answering)
Sarah?

SARAH
(on the phone)
James, I've been thinking. I believe in you. I want to give you a chance to prove yourself.

JAMES
(hopeful)
Really?

SARAH
(determined)
Yes. I'll put you on a probationary period. If you can perform, I'll offer you the job. What do you say?

JAMES
(grateful)
Thank you, Sarah. I won't let you down.

INT. OFFICE BUILDING - DAY

James starts his new job, eager to prove himself. He works hard and focuses on his tasks. His coworkers notice the change and offer support.

INT. HR OFFICE - WEEKS LATER

Sarah sits at her desk, reviewing James' performance reports. She smiles to herself, proud of his progress.

INT. OFFICE BUILDING - END OF DAY

James leaves the office building, feeling a sense of accomplishment. He glances at his phone, seeing a message from Sarah.

SARAH
(text)
Congratulations, James. You've done it. Welcome to the team.

FADE OUT.
